ai.description: *Hypnale hypnale* reaches 30–45 cm. It is brown or grey with dark triangular lateral spots and a distinctively upturned, fleshy, scale-covered snout tip. The tail is often yellow or reddish.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Hypnale hypnale* is the distinct, upturned, fleshy appendage at the tip of its snout, which is absent in other Indian pit vipers.
ai.habitat: The Hump-nosed Moccasin inhabits rainforests, evergreen forests, and rubber or cardamom plantations, typically ranging from sea level up to 1,500 meters in elevation.
ai.behavior: The Hump-nosed Moccasin is primarily nocturnal, often remaining motionless among leaf litter to ambush small lizards, frogs, and rodents that pass within its striking range.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hypnale hypnale* is ovoviviparous, producing litters of 4–17 young. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, with births often recorded between March and July.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hypnale hypnale* is found in the Western Ghats and the wet zones of Sri Lanka, typically inhabiting rainforests and plantations from sea level up to 1,500 meters.
